item.title: When Should You Normalize or Scale Rewards in Reinforcement Learning: Criteria and Common Methods
item.description: The reward scale directly affects the numerical scale of returns, V/Q targets, TD errors, or policy update signals, and therefore affects the stability of loss functions and gradient updates. If the reward scale is too large or fluctuates too violently, it is more likely to cause issues such as overly large value losses, unstable gradients, and training oscillations.

item.title: What Does the Reward Function Depend On: \(R(s)\)、\(R(s')\)、\(R(s,a)\) and \(R(s,a,s')\)?
item.description: The immediate reward returned by the environment during a transition can depend on different pieces of information: the current state , the next state , the state-action pair , or the full transition .

item.title: Deconstructing Reward in RL
item.description: In Reinforcement Learning (RL), “Reward” is a core concept that seems simple but is extremely prone to confusion in both theory and practice.

item.title: RL Chart Reading: Stable = Converged = Optimal?
item.description: In model training: 1. If variable values stabilize, is this always good news? 2. If the curve is stable, does it count as converged? 3. If it has converged, can I say it’s optimal? 4. If it’s optimal, does it perform well?
